v17.t: RPM, CPM, CPC: which number should you watch?
v17.d:
RPM, CPM or CPC: which number should you actually watch?

CPC is what one click pays. CPM is what 1,000 ad impressions pay. RPM is what 1,000 pageviews earn with every ad included, so it is the number that reflects your layout, your traffic mix and your buyers. Track it weekly and ask why whenever it moves.

v18.t: Why traffic from some countries pays more
v18.d:
Why does the same article earn more from one country than another?

Advertisers set budgets per market. Where more of them compete for the same reader, bids are higher. That is demand, not your content quality. Chasing one country rarely works. Viewable placements, a fast page and more buyers in the auction raise what every visitor earns.

v20.t: Consent banner not loading? Your EU ads are unfilled.
v20.d:
Is your consent banner loading on every page?

Without a consent choice, no personalised ad can serve to an EU or UK visitor. Buyers skip or bid very low and the slot often stays empty. The usual causes are a caching plugin that strips the script, a banner that loads after the ads, a security plugin blocking the domain, or a tag lost in a theme update. Check consent coverage in your reports.

v21.t: Ad refresh: free money or a policy problem?
v21.d:
Is ad refresh free money or a policy problem?

It depends on how it is done. Refresh only where the ad is actually viewable, only after a real minimum interval, and declared to buyers as refreshed inventory. Buyers bid a little less for refreshed impressions, so it wins on long reads with sticky slots and loses on short pages. Test it slot by slot.

v23.t: Why your AdSense estimate changed before payday
v23.d:
Why is your AdSense balance lower than the estimate you watched all month?

The daily number is an estimate. Around the 3rd, Google finalises the previous month and removes invalid clicks, bot impressions and activity that broke a policy. Usually that is a small share. The payment then goes out between the 21st and the 26th if you passed the threshold.

v24.t: Your mobile layout earns most of your money. Treat it that way.
v24.d:
Was your ad layout designed on a desktop but read on phones?

On a phone there is no sidebar. The ads that earn are in the reading flow and the sticky anchor at the bottom, while top banners get scrolled past in a second. Reserve the space so nothing jumps, keep ads under 30% of the screen height, and test on a real phone.

v25.t: Price floors: the setting that can raise or kill your income
v25.d:
Could one setting in Ad Manager be emptying half your ad slots?

A price floor is the minimum bid you accept. Too low and buyers pay less than they would. Too high and nobody wins, so the slot stays empty. Income rises as the floor rises, until fill rate falls off a cliff, and that peak is different for every slot, device and country. A managed setup reviews floors weekly.

v27.t: Ads not showing? Six causes, in order
v27.d:
Ads not showing on your site?

Check six causes in order: the ad code is missing or broken, your own ad blocker is on, a policy limit sits on the account, the site is not added or still under review, no consent was given on EU or UK traffic, or simply no buyer bid on that impression. Empty slots on some pages are normal. Empty slots everywhere are a setup problem.

v28.t: sellers.json: the other file buyers check
v28.d:
Did you know ads.txt has a twin?

ads.txt lives on your site and lists who may sell your ad space. sellers.json lives on the seller's side and lists who they sell for. Together they let a buyer trace every impression back to a real publisher, which is what lets bigger budgets reach smaller sites. Keep your business name and domain consistent everywhere.

v29.t: Thanksgiving: traffic dips, bids do not
v29.d:
Does Thanksgiving hurt your ad income?

Pageviews on many sites dip for a day while people cook, travel and shop, then jump on Black Friday and the weekend. Advertisers keep spending through the dip, so RPM often holds or rises even while visits fall. Watch RPM, make sure the site loads on a phone, every slot fills, and nothing updates tonight.

v30.t: Black Friday: what to watch in your reports today
v30.d:
What should you watch in your ad reports on Black Friday?

Four numbers in this order: fill rate (is every slot selling), page RPM (is each view paying more), viewability (are the ads seen) and page speed (is the site holding up). If fill drops, check ads.txt and the consent banner first. If speed drops, a plugin probably updated itself. And do not add slots today to catch the wave.

v31.t: News pages spike. Evergreen pages pay the rent.
v31.d:
Is your site built on spikes or on rent?

A news post earns most of what it will ever earn in 48 hours. An evergreen guide earns a little every day for years, and usually more per view, because readers stay longer, scroll further and see more ads. Build the archive, then make sure every page is set up to earn.

v32.t: Never click your own ads. Here is what Google sees.
v32.d:
Have you ever clicked your own ads to test them?

Asking friends to click, click exchange groups, click farm traffic and refresh scripts on hidden ads all count as invalid activity. The cost runs from a deduction to a disabled account that rarely comes back.
